title: Host & Hostess Gifts
headline: Host & Hostess Gifts (Because Wine Is Not a Personality, Darling)
seo_title: Host & Hostess Gifts: 8 Ideas She'll Actually Remember | Looks Like Luxe
description: Host and hostess gifts that go way beyond a bottle of wine: a champagne saber, a cocktail smoker, a truffle oil duo, a bitters trio and more. Elegant, giftable and not another candle.
intro: There are two kinds of dinner guests. The ones who arrive with a thoughtful, beautiful gift, and the ones who arrive with a bottle of wine they clearly grabbed from the gas station on the way over.
I'm not here to judge. (I am a little bit here to judge.)
A host or hostess gift is the smallest possible way to say "thank you for feeding me and letting me stay until 11:45." It should feel like you thought about her, not like you panicked in an aisle.

So I built a list of eight gifts that say you have taste and a pulse. Every one has real reviews and a rating of 4.5 stars or higher at the time I checked. Some are bold, some are practical, and one involves a very dramatic way to open champagne.
Grab your plus-one, darling. Let's go be invited back.
disclosure: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases, which means if you tap a link and buy, I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. Prices and availability live on Amazon.

products.name: BARE BARREL Mixology Bartender Kit, 16-Piece Cocktail Set
products.best_for: The host who "just throws a few drinks together" and secretly owns three cocktail books
copy: A full bartender kit in one box: shaker, tools and a stand, so the cocktail hour looks like it came with a bartender.
It has a 4.8-star rating from more than 600 reviewers, and it turns a drinks cart into a whole moment. It's the gift that gets used at the very next party.
Verdict: the host who loves to entertain will use this every single weekend.

products.name: Whiskey and Cocktail Smoker Kit with Torch, 6 Wood Chip Flavors and 2 Glasses
products.best_for: The host who takes party tricks very seriously
copy: Wait, you can SMOKE a cocktail? Yes. You can. You pop a glass over a drink, add a little smoke, and everyone at the table says "how did you do that?"
More than 6,700 reviewers have given this kit a 4.6-star rating, and it comes with glasses and wood chip flavors so it is ready to gift straight out of the box.
Verdict: it's theater for the person who loves to put on a show.

products.name: Bamboo Charcuterie Board and Cheese Knife Set
products.best_for: The host whose cheese plate is a love language
copy: A real board, real knives and a slide-out drawer, which means no more serving brie on a dinner plate.
It has a 4.8-star rating from more than 12,000 reviewers, which tells you everybody's mother-in-law has quietly approved of it.
Verdict: it's classic, beautiful, and she will use it for every party for years.

products.name: Fox Knives Champagne Saber (Sciabola del Sommelier)
products.best_for: The host who has strong opinions about New Year's Eve
copy: Yes, that is a sword. Yes, you use it to open champagne. It's called sabrage, it's a tradition, and it will make everyone gasp.
It's the biggest splurge on this list, and a 4.7-star rating from hundreds of reviewers backs it up. Please watch a tutorial and do it outside. We love you and we love your windows.
Verdict: the gift that gets talked about at brunch the next day.

products.name: NEST New York Scented Classic Candle, Bamboo
products.best_for: The host with a beautiful home and a very good nose
copy: I said not another candle, and then I included one. This is the exception. A Nest candle is the quiet, classy hostess gift that looks like you spent a lot of time thinking.
It's loved by more than 1,100 reviewers at a 4.6-star rating, and the bamboo scent is fresh enough for any room.
Verdict: the safe choice, but make it expensive-looking.

products.name: Bitters Triple Play Cocktail Bitters Variety Set
products.best_for: The host who makes an old fashioned like it's a hobby
copy: Three small bottles that turn one drink into a better drink. This is the kind of gift a cocktail person would never buy for herself.
More than 2,300 reviewers have given it a 4.8-star rating. It's small, it's giftable, and it makes a very good add-on to a bottle of something nice.
Verdict: tiny gift, big bartender energy.

products.name: BASSO 1904 Infused Extra Virgin Olive Oil Gift Set
products.best_for: The host who owns a pasta maker and talks about it
copy: A set of infused olive oils in a gift-ready box. Dip some bread, drizzle some pasta, and suddenly dinner feels like it was cooked in Italy.
More than 1,200 reviewers rate it 4.6 stars, and it's the kind of pantry treat people actually finish.
Verdict: a foodie gift that doesn't need any explaining.

products.name: TruffleHunter Black and White Truffle Olive Oil Duo
products.best_for: The host who has a pasta night and calls it "just a little something"
copy: Truffle oil, two ways, because one truffle is a snack and two is a lifestyle. A drizzle on pasta, eggs or popcorn makes any plate taste like it came from a restaurant with a waitlist.
It has a 4.5-star rating from more than 7,300 reviewers, so this one isn't a trend. It's a pantry glow-up.
Verdict: the gift that makes her say, "oh, I can't wait to use this."

interludes.3: A good host gift says thank you. A great one says you were invited back.
interludes.6: Bring the wine if you must. Bring something memorable if you can.

outro: And that's the list: eight host and hostess gifts that take you from "nice guest" to "please come again."

If you take one thing from this guide, let it be this. The best host gift is something she'd never buy for herself, wrapped up so it feels like a little treat. Add a handwritten note and you've won the whole evening.
Until the next dinner party, darling.
